analysis.title: Observability Technical Lead
analysis.fit_rationale: Strong alignment in observability, APM, and performance engineering with deep expertise in CA APM, Dynatrace, and Splunk, plus Python automation and ETL skills. Gaps in modern cloud-native observability stack (OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Prometheus, Kubernetes) and SRE practices (SLOs, error budgets) are partially offset by foundational AWS and project experience.
strengths: Expert-level APM and performance engineering with CA APM and Dynatrace, directly relevant to observability platform leadership.
Proven Python automation and ETL skills for telemetry data processing, validation, and anomaly detection.
Experience with Splunk as a data source and capacity reporting, aligning with observability data integration.
Strong capacity planning and forecasting background, supporting reliability and proactive operations.
Consulting and mentoring experience from CA Technologies, suitable for technical leadership without direct authority.
gaps: No professional experience with OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, Loki, or VictoriaMetrics.
Limited Kubernetes and container observability experience; foundational AWS only.
No explicit SRE practice implementation (SLIs, SLOs, error budgets) in professional roles.
AIOps and automation at scale (eBPF, continuous profiling) not evidenced.
Current role is capacity-focused; observability leadership scope may be broader than current responsibilities.
tailoring_plan: Rewrite resume summary to lead with 'Observability and Performance Engineer' and quantify APM experience (e.g., 'managed Dynatrace for enterprise environments'). Add a 'Technical Skills' section listing Splunk, Dynatrace, CA APM, Python, SQL, and mention foundational AWS. In experience bullets, reframe capacity monitoring as 'observability and telemetry analysis' and highlight Splunk integration. Add a 'Projects' section for the AWS lakehouse and HorizonScale to demonstrate cloud and forecasting skills. In cover letter, explicitly address OpenTelemetry and Kubernetes gaps by expressing eagerne
